newsitem.title: USA: Hess launches derivatives oil trading unit.
newsitem.headline: Hess launches derivatives oil trading unit.

text.p: Amerada Hess Corp, seeking to improve its ability to manage price risk in volatile oil markets, has launched a new joint venture oil derivatives trading company.
"It's a propietary joint venture trading company to manage financial commodity risk," said Carl Tursi, spokesman at New York-based Hess, without giving further details.
Industry sources said the new company, Hess Energy Trading Co, will deal in derivatives such as options or swaps as well as in physical commodities, including crude oil and refined products.
The sources said the new company is made up of two traders recruited from J. Aron, Goldman Sachs oil trading arm, and a third trader already with Hess. The traders will hold stock in the new company.

Traders welcomed the Hess foray into the world of oil derivatives, saying it would add liquidity to a sector of the oil market that has contracted in recent years amid regulatory risk related to the launch of cleaner motor fuels.

The U.S. derivative market itself has shrunk, the traders said, and is dominated by big Wall Street players like Morgan Stanley Group Inc, JP Morgan & Co and Phibro, the commmodities trading arm of Salomon Inc.
Sources said Hess will join other relatively recent entrants into the derivatives realm from the energy industry like Koch Oil Co and Trammochem.
"It's good news. We need the liquidity," said one refined products broker referring to Hess's new unit.
-- Oliver Ludwig New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1633
